Kuvitus: kevyen liikenteen silta joen yl: Illustration: a footbridge for pedestrians and cyclists over a river on a summer day. In the middle of the bridge a young person drops a stone over the railing, and a friend on the bank films the fall with a phone. The stone is drawn at five positions at equal time intervals: the gaps grow downwards in the ratio 1 : 3 : 5 : 7, and the blue velocity arrow beside the stone grows by the same amount each time. The measuring rod on the right shows five heights: its alternately shaded parts are the distances travelled by the stone, and they grow in the ratio 1 : 3 : 5 : 7. At the lowest position the stone hits the water and the water splashes. The scale is not exact, but the ratios of the gaps are.
Kaavakuva kahdesta kärrystä, jotka on ku: Schematic picture of two carts photographed at one-second intervals, the gaps to scale. At the top the cart starts from rest and accelerates: the gaps grow, the blue velocity arrow grows by the same amount every second, and the orange acceleration arrow points in the direction of motion and stays the same length. At the bottom the cart slows down: the gaps get shorter, the velocity arrow gets shorter, and the acceleration arrow points against the motion; in the last picture the cart is at rest for a moment, but the acceleration arrow is still the same.
Kaavakuva kahdesta (t,v)-kuvaajasta, ei: Schematic picture of two (t,v) graphs, with no numerical values. On the left a straight line rises from the initial velocity v0, and two points chosen on the line bound a triangle: the time interval Δt and the change in velocity Δv, whose ratio is the acceleration a. On the right three lines from the same initial velocity: the rising line is acceleration a greater than zero, the horizontal line acceleration zero, that is, uniform motion, and the falling line acceleration less than zero.
Kaavakuva (t,x)-kuvaajasta, ei lukuarvoj: Schematic picture of a (t,x) graph, with no numerical values. The graph of a cart accelerating from rest is a curve bending upwards that gets steeper all the time. A tangent, that is, a line that just touches the curve at that point, is drawn as a dashed line at the point P of the curve. Two points far apart are chosen on the tangent, and their time interval Δt and change in position Δx form a triangle. The slope of the tangent, Δx divided by Δt, is the cart's instantaneous velocity at the moment that P corresponds to.
Kaavakuva (t,v)-kuvaajasta, ei lukuarvoj: Schematic picture of a (t,v) graph, with no numerical values. The velocity grows in a straight line from the initial velocity v0 at time 0 to the velocity v at time t. The region under the line is divided into two parts: a blue rectangle whose height is v0 and width t, and on top of it an orange triangle whose height is the growth of velocity at and width t. The area of the rectangle is v0 times t and the area of the triangle is half of a t times t; together they are the displacement Δx.
(t,s)-kuvaaja mittakaavassa: pudotetun t: (t,s) graph to scale: the distance s fallen by a dropped steel ball, from nine frames of a video at intervals of 0.05 seconds, from time 0 to 0.40 seconds. The points: 0.002; 0.018; 0.065; 0.128; 0.223; 0.338; 0.477; 0.646 and 0.832 metres. No curve has been fitted to the points.
(t,v)-kuvaaja mittakaavassa: potkulaudan: (t,v) graph to scale: the velocity of a kick scooter grows steadily. The line starts from the velocity 2.0 metres per second at time 0 and ends at the velocity 7.0 metres per second at time 5.0 seconds.
(t,x)-kuvaaja mittakaavassa: levosta kii: (t,x) graph to scale: the position of a cart accelerating from rest is a curve bending upwards from time 0 to time 7 seconds. A tangent is drawn as a dashed line at the point at time 4.0 seconds, at the position 8.0 metres. The tangent crosses the time axis at time 2.0 seconds and passes through the point (6.0 s; 16 m).
(t,v)-kuvaaja mittakaavassa: sähköpotkul: (t,v) graph to scale: the velocity of an electric scooter grows steadily. The line starts from the velocity 2.0 metres per second at time 0 and ends at the velocity 6.0 metres per second at time 8.0 seconds.
